note: Leads are not verified parsers. Ranks are assigned only among verified paths.

leads.name: sql-formatter
leads.reason: Formatter that returns text; no syntax tree.

leads.name: node-sql-parser
leads.reason: new Parser().astify(sql, {database}) returns an AST (type select/insert, from, columns, where, groupby, orderby).

leads.name: libpg-query
leads.family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
leads.reason: parse(sql) returns the PostgreSQL parse tree from a WASM build of libpg_query 18. Rechecked in round 2: the package runs libpg_query compiled to WebAssembly (wasm/index.cjs loads the module), and Node V8 coverage reports only JavaScript ranges, never the C source lines inside the module; the npm build ships no DWARF or source map that would map module offsets back to the pinned C files. A C-coverage route would need a separately instrumented libpg_query build, which would no longer be the published package bytes. The parser-source coverage gate cannot be met, so it stays a coverage blocker; the C library itself is selected in the C cell.

leads.name: pgsql-ast-parser
leads.reason: parse(sql) returns a typed AST (select/insert statements) from its own nearley grammar.

leads.name: @zeit/cosmosdb-query
leads.reason: A SQL parser and executor for Cosmos DB (0.7.2, MIT, 2021). Its documented API compiles a query and executes it over in-memory items; the Cosmos DB SQL grammar (lib/parser.js) has no INSERT statement and its JOIN is an intra-document iteration, so the INSERT control cannot be parsed and no syntax-tree API is documented. Engine/dialect mismatch; not a candidate.

leads.name: pgsql-parser
leads.family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
leads.reason: pgsql-parser 18.3.5 (MIT) parses through its dependency libpg-query 18.2.4 (WASM) and adds a deparser; same family and coverage blocker as libpg-query (V8 coverage does not report the C lines inside the WebAssembly module).

leads.name: pg-query-emscripten
leads.family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
leads.reason: pg-query-emscripten 5.1.0 (MIT) wraps an Emscripten build of libpg_query. Round 2 inspected the tarball (sha256 d598a66f...): pg_query.js is wasm2js output (it defines a JavaScript WebAssembly polyfill and runs the translated module as about 2.5 MB of generated JavaScript), and pg_query_wasm.js embeds the module as a base64 data URI. V8 coverage would report lines of translated machine code, not the libpg_query C sources, and no source map is shipped; same family and blocker as libpg-query.

leads.name: plpgsql-parser
leads.family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
leads.reason: plpgsql-parser 18.6.6 (MIT) parses SQL and PL/pgSQL through libpg-query 18.2.4 (WASM); same family and coverage blocker as libpg-query.

leads.name: @derekstride/tree-sitter-sql
leads.reason: tree-sitter-sql 0.3.13 (MIT) is a tree-sitter grammar whose generated parser is C (src/parser.c) loaded as a node-addon-api binding (node-gyp-build) by the separate tree-sitter runtime package. The concrete syntax tree could give the summary, but the parser runs as native code: V8 coverage cannot see it, and parser-source coverage plus AFL++ feedback would need the addon rebuilt with LLVM coverage and AFL++ instrumentation inside Node. Not attempted in round 2; it stays an unrun lead with that blocker.

leads.name: @dbml/core
leads.family: DBML parser with SQL DDL importers
leads.reason: @dbml/core 12.1.0 parses DBML and imports SQL DDL (CREATE TABLE) into a schema model; it does not parse SELECT or INSERT statements into a syntax tree. Schema-only, excluded per the SQL protocol.

leads.name: @guanmingchiu/sqlparser-ts
leads.reason: WASM build of sqlparser-rs (0.63.0, Apache-2.0; dist/index.cjs loads a .wasm module). V8 coverage does not report the Rust source lines inside the module, so the parser-source coverage gate cannot be met with the JavaScript harness pattern; the Rust crate itself is selected in the Rust cell.

leads.name: sql-parser-cst
leads.reason: parse(sql, {dialect}) returns a concrete syntax tree.

leads.name: dt-sql-parser
leads.reason: ANTLR4-based parsers per dialect, returning ANTLR parse trees.

leads.name: js-sql-parser
leads.reason: js-sql-parser 1.6.0 (ISC; jison MySQL grammar, documented as 'select grammar'). parse() returns an AST for the SELECT control, but the INSERT control fails at the first token after INSERT: "Parse error on line 1 ... Expecting '(', 'SELECT', got 'IDENTIFIER'". The grammar covers SELECT only.

leads.name: @clickhouse/parser
leads.reason: @clickhouse/parser 0.3.0 (Apache-2.0). parse() returns a ClickHouse AST for the SELECT control, but for the INSERT control it returns only {type: 'InsertQuery', table, columns, format: 'Values'}: as in ClickHouse, the VALUES data is left to the input-format reader and is not parsed, so the row count and literals cannot be read. Fails the INSERT summary.

leads.name: @materializeinc/sql-parser
leads.reason: @materializeinc/sql-parser 26.50.1 is a WebAssembly build of Materialize's Rust SQL parser (mz_sql_parser_wasm_bg.wasm). Its LICENSE is the Materialize Business Source License 1.1, not an open-source license, and V8 coverage would not report the Rust source lines inside the module. Excluded.

leads.name: sqlite-parser
leads.reason: sqliteParser(sql) returns a SQLite AST (statement list with select/insert variants) from its PEG.js grammar; minified without a source map.

leads.name: @appland/sql-parser
leads.reason: AppLand-maintained fork of sqlite-parser (1.5.1, 2022) with a modified PEG.js grammar and the same AST shape. Not byte-identical: the minified generated parser is 127,259 bytes against 109,981, and about 51% of sqlite-parser 1.0.1's statement fragments occur unchanged in it (43% of the fork's); the wrapper files differ only in the version banner.

leads.name: @pgsql/parser
leads.family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
leads.reason: WASM build of libpg_query (1.6.4, MIT; ./wasm/index.cjs). Same coverage blocker as libpg-query: V8 coverage does not report C source lines inside the WebAssembly module.

leads.name: sql-parser-mistic
leads.reason: sql-parser-mistic 1.2.3 (MIT, 2019) is a fork of sql-parser. Both controls fail in the lexer at the statement terminator: "NOTHING CONSUMED: Stopped at - ';'".

leads.name: postgresql-eslint-parser
leads.family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
leads.reason: postgresql-eslint-parser 0.6.2 (MIT) is an ESLint parser that parses through @libpg-query/parser (WASM build of libpg_query); same family and coverage blocker as libpg-query.

leads.name: pg-query-parser
leads.family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
leads.reason: pg-query-parser 0.3.0 (BSD-3-Clause, 2021) parses through its dependency pg-query-native, a node-gyp addon over an old libpg_query (PostgreSQL 10). The parser runs as native C inside the addon; V8 coverage cannot see it, and a coverage or AFL++ build would have to rebuild the addon with instrumentation. Not attempted in round 2; libpg_query is selected in the C cell.

leads.name: @griffithswaite/ts-plsql-parser
leads.reason: @griffithswaite/ts-plsql-parser 1.1.1 (BSD-3-Clause), the grammars-v4 Oracle PL/SQL grammar on the antlr4 runtime. Both controls report a syntax error: the SELECT control at 'AS' in the table alias ('line 2:15 mismatched input 'AS' expecting {<EOF>, '/', ';'}'; Oracle has no AS before a table alias) and the INSERT control at the second VALUES row ('line 2:28 mismatched input ','').

leads.name: sql-parser
leads.reason: sql-parser 0.5.0 (2015, CoffeeScript lexer and jison grammar). Both controls fail in the lexer at the statement terminator: "NOTHING CONSUMED: Stopped at - ';'". The controls are fixed and end with ';', so the path cannot be verified.

leads.name: @openobserve/node-sql-parser
leads.reason: @openobserve/node-sql-parser 0.1.5 (Apache-2.0) is a republish of an older node-sql-parser: its package.json repository and homepage point to taozhi8833998/node-sql-parser and its README is node-sql-parser's. Comparing the grammar sources embedded in the shipped source maps, 88.2% of its postgresql.pegjs lines (38,021 of 43,123) are identical to node-sql-parser 5.4.0's (81.3% of the selected path's 46,756). Its only addition is an undocumented datafusionsql build. Both controls parse, but as a republished snapshot of the selected node-sql-parser lineage it is not counted as a separate path.

leads.name: @joe-re/sql-parser
leads.reason: @joe-re/sql-parser 1.7.1 (GPLv2), an early node-sql-parser fork used by sql-language-server. The SELECT control parses; the INSERT control fails at the second row ('Expected "--", "/*", ";", [ \t\n\r], or end of input but "," found').

leads.name: sql-ddl-to-json-schema
leads.reason: DDL-only converter; cannot parse SELECT.

leads.name: node-sqlparser
leads.reason: node-sqlparser 1.0.4 (GPL-2.0, 2018). Both controls fail at the statement terminator ('... or end of input but ";" found').

leads.name: sql-surveyor
leads.reason: sql-surveyor 1.4.1 (MIT) returns an analysis summary (output columns, referenced columns and tables, tokens), not a syntax tree; its grammar lives in the separate antlr4ts-sql package. The survey has no join, grouping, ordering, row or literal structure (for example SUM(o.total) is reported with table name 'SUM(o'), so the summary cannot be read from it.

leads.name: sqllens
leads.family: sqllens ANTLR4 grammars (PostgreSQL grammar forked from antlr/grammars-v4)
leads.reason: parse(sql, dialect) returns {ast, errors, cst}; the lowered IR marks INSERT as unsupported, so the summary is read from the documented CST (full ANTLR4 parse tree).

leads.name: oracle-sql-parser
leads.reason: oracle-sql-parser 0.1.0 (MIT) parses Oracle DDL only: both controls fail at the first keyword ('Expected "alter", "create", "drop" ... but "S" found'). Schema-only, excluded per the SQL protocol.

leads.name: rawsql-ts
leads.family: rawsql-ts hand-written tokenizer and recursive-descent parser
leads.reason: SqlParser.parse / parseMany return typed query models (SimpleSelectQuery, InsertQuery with a ValuesQuery).

leads.name: @sgress454/node-sql-parser
leads.reason: @sgress454/node-sql-parser 5.4.0-fork.2 is a fork of node-sql-parser 5.4.0 'with bug-fixes for sqlite'. The postgresql.pegjs grammar embedded in its source map is byte-identical to the selected node-sql-parser 5.4.0 path (46,756 of 46,756 lines); the rebuilt bundles differ only by the fork's other grammar changes. Excluded as a duplicate of the selected path.

leads.name: @questdb/sql-parser
leads.reason: parseToAst(sql) returns {ast, errors}: typed select/insert statements from the package's Chevrotain parser for QuestDB SQL.

leads.name: @tableland/sqlparser
leads.reason: @tableland/sqlparser 1.4.1 ships a Go parser compiled to WebAssembly (main.wasm loaded through Go's wasm_exec glue in esm/out.js) and has no license field in package.json. V8 coverage does not report the Go source lines inside the module; not a candidate in this round.

leads.name: @deepnote/sql-parser
leads.reason: @deepnote/sql-parser 3.0.0 (GPLv2) is a fork of @joe-re/sql-parser. The SELECT control parses; the INSERT control fails at the second row ('Expected "--", "/*", ";", [ \t\n\r], or end of input but "," found').

leads.name: @saralsql/tsql-parser
leads.reason: analyze(sql) returns {ast, issues, ...}; the Program AST has SelectStatement and InsertStatement nodes from the package's own T-SQL lexer and parser.

leads.name: @florajs/sql-parser
leads.reason: @florajs/sql-parser 4.0.0 (GPL-2.0), a fork of an early node-sql-parser PEG.js grammar for SELECT. The SELECT control fails at the first qualified column ('Expected "--", "/*", "UNION", [ \t\n\r], or end of input but "." found') and the INSERT control fails at the column list ('Expected [A-Za-z0-9_:] but ")" found').

leads.name: sqljs
leads.reason: sqljs 0.0.0-6 (2015) is a pre-release with no license field; its README says the npm package is not the supported install path and directs users to build from git. No pinnable licensed release; not a candidate.

leads.name: sql-ast
leads.reason: sql-ast 0.3.0 (MIT) parses MySQL schema statements; the SELECT control fails with 'Unknown statement SELECT'. Schema-only, excluded per the SQL protocol.
